prerequisites: Minimal familiarity as a common user with a computer

learning_outcomes.text: Locate computer science within engineering disciplines.
Understand the fundamentals of the binary system to comprehend information representation in computers.
Identify the hardware components that constitute a computer system, as well as their interconnection in networks, and understand their basic operation.
Distinguish the main peripherals used in a computer system and specifically in the field of engineering.
Classify the different types of software used in a computer system.
Identify and classify different types of computer systems and their application areas.
Understand the concept of algorithm and the process of problem abstraction in programming.
Identify the program development process and its location within the general Software Engineering process.
Recognize the elementary data structures provided by a structured programming language.
Handle the elementary control structures of a structured programming language.
Abstract operations.
Design small applications to solve elementary problems in collaborative work environments.
Know the main functions performed by an operating system.
Analyze which services the operating system provides to programs and end-users.
Identify the main operating systems used in professional engineering environments and utilize their main user-level services.
Know the main functions performed by a database management system.
Create data models for simple problems.
Use basic expressions to retrieve and modify information stored in a database.
Identify which database management systems are used in professional engineering environments.
Identify the main application programs used in professional engineering environments.

syllabus_topics: INT - Introduction
Overview of computer science, in the context of other engineering disciplines
Structure and functioning of a computer
Representation of information in a computer
PRO - Introduction to programming
Problem abstraction for programming: fundamental concepts
Variables, expressions, assignment
Use of console input/output
Handling basic control flow structures: sequential, alternative, and repetitive
Definition and use of subprograms and functions. Variable scope
File input/output
Basic data types and structures
Program development processes. From high-level to processor execution. Compiled languages and interpreted languages.
BD - Introduction to databases
Concept of database
Fundamentals of the relational data model
Performing queries and modifications
Database Management Systems in professional engineering environments
HSW - Hardware and software components of a computer system
Structure and functioning of a computer: Von Neumann Architecture and machine language
Peripheral devices
Interconnection of systems: types, mechanisms, and applications
Types of software: system software and application software
Types of computer systems and their application areas
SO - Introduction to operating systems
Concept and functions performed by an operating system
Interface and services offered to programs
Interface and services offered to users
Operating systems used in professional engineering environments
Introduction to tools in the practice laboratory (1h)
Spreadsheet as a tool (3h)
Programming (18h)
Design, implementation, and exploitation of a database (6h)

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment of practical exams (Excel, Access, Programming)

assessment_rules: The ordinary assessment consists of a theory part (50%) and a practical part (50%). A minimum score of 4 out of 10 in both parts is required; otherwise, the final grade is a fail, calculated as the average of both parts with a maximum of 4.5 points. To pass, the final grade must be at least 5 out of 10. Uncompleted evaluable activities count as zero; if they account for more than 50% of the total grade, the final grade will be "Not presented". There are no recovery exams for any evaluable part. The extraordinary assessment requires at least 5 out of 10 in both the theoretical and practical exams, each weighted 50%; otherwise, the final grade is a fail, calculated as the average of both parts with a maximum of 4.5 points. Students who fail a previous call but have a grade of 5 or higher in theory or practice do not need to repeat that part in the second call; partial practical scores (Excel, Access, Programming) of 7 or higher are also retained.
